machines.name: Automatic Chocolate Shell Moulding Line
machines.summary: Classic shell line that forms, fills, and backs chocolates — including whole-nut and liquid centers — at up to 1,500 kg/h.
machines.description:
Choose shell moulding when the center is too fluid, too chunky, or too delicate for a one-shot deposit. The mould is filled, inverted, and cooled to leave a shell; filling goes in next; a chocolate back closes the piece before the final cool and demould.

The MKSL-A family spans 450 to 1,500 kg/h at 12–15 shots/min, with published power anywhere from 100 kW to 350 kW depending on the cooling and auxiliary package. Optional stations cover a second filling, biscuit or wafer feed, whole hazelnuts, granules, and toy inserts. Line length is quoted from 24 m upward, so floor space is part of the first conversation.
features: Traditional shell, fill, and back sequence
Liquid, caramel, jelly, and cream centers
Whole-nut and granule stations as options

US plants use this one-shot frame when a single depositor pass has to create the shell and the center together.
